title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from neighbouring pages): G is a GL_2-type group scheme, SG its SL_2 part and PG its projective quotient. T_rho is a torus, N'_sigma is a torus-normalizer-type group, and delta_rho, delta_sigma are 'determinant' characters to G_m. epsilon_sigma : N'_sigma -> mu_2 is the sign/component character. The goal is a group M_{rho,sigma} with a homomorphism Theta : M -> G. It is to be presented as a contracted product M = (R_{rho,sigma} x SG)/mu_2, eqs. (102)-(103). This is the same pattern as GL_2 = (G_m x SL_2)/mu_2. Page 435 computes R_{rho,sigma} as a fibre product and states (105): the square formed by R -> T_{rho,sigma} (canonical), R -> G_m (lambda), T -> G_m (chi) and G_m -> G_m (lambda |-> lambda^2) is cartesian. So R is the pullback of the Kummer double cover along chi. In other words, R is the group of pairs (t, lambda) with chi(t) = lambda^2: the 'square root of chi' cover of T. This page draws the consequence as diagram (106).

- Rows: two exact sequences, 1 -> mu_2 -> R -> T -> 1 and 1 -> mu_2 -> G_m -> G_m -> 1 (squaring).
- The vertical maps are kappa : R -> G_m and chi : T -> G_m.
- Columns: the kernels give SR := Ker(kappa), and SR is isomorphic to T^+ := Ker(chi).

This is a standard property of a cartesian square of epimorphisms with the same kernel. Grothendieck calls it an explicitation of a 'fait surprenant' (footnote *): the analogous diagrams (95) of an earlier page are obtained from this one. The summary (107)-(108) lists what the construction yields, all in terms of the data (T_rho, N'_sigma, delta_rho, delta_sigma, epsilon_sigma):

- the group T_{rho,sigma}, with homomorphisms chi : T -> G_m and (epsilon_3, epsilon_2) : T -> mu_2 x mu_2;
- through (105)-(106), the groups R_{rho,sigma} and SR_{rho,sigma}, with SR isomorphic to T^+;
- the 'connected' variants T^0 = Ker(T -> mu_2 x mu_2), R^0, and SR^0, with SR^0 isomorphic to T^{+0}.

The next page then realises T_{rho,sigma} as a subgroup of T_0 x T_rho x N'_sigma, cut out by delta_rho(a) = epsilon' delta_sigma(b) with epsilon'^2 = 1. Overall this is bookkeeping for building explicit GL_2-valued representations of the groups (presumably triangle-type / loop-equation groups) from tori and torus normalizers.
errors: No mathematical error. SR ≅ T^+ follows correctly from the cartesian square (105), since both horizontal maps are mu_2-torsors with the same kernel.
Minor notational instability: the mu_2 x mu_2-valued map is written (epsilon_3, epsilon_2) here but (epsilon_3, epsilon_1) on the next page.
The page uses R/SR and script-T/T^+ loosely.

ideas.what: Pulling back the Kummer sequence 1->mu_2->G_m->G_m->1 along a character chi : T -> G_m. This gives a central mu_2-extension R of T, whose 'special' part SR = Ker(kappa) is identified with Ker(chi).
ideas.modern_name: Pullback of the Kummer extension / square-root cover of a character (as in metaplectic or spin-type double covers)
ideas.where_published: general techniques in SGA 3; not this specific construction

ideas.what: Presenting a subgroup of GL_2 as a contracted product (R x SL_2)/mu_2, analogous to GL_2 = (G_m x SL_2)/mu_2. R is built from a torus T_rho and a normalizer-type group N'_sigma, together with sign characters to mu_2 x mu_2 and the 'connected' variants T^0, R^0, SR^0.
ideas.modern_name: Contracted products / central extensions; normalizers of tori in GL_2

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine diagram chase and inventory of objects: a cartesian square with the Kummer sequence and the resulting kernel isomorphism. It is bookkeeping within a larger construction, with nothing new beyond its local role in the notes.
transcription_corrections: The left vertical map R_{rho,sigma} -> G_m is labelled kappa (κ), not π; this matches 'R_{rho,sigma} --κ--> G_m' on the next page.
In the diagram the right-hand group is script T_{rho,sigma} (\mathcal{T}), with its kernel T^+_{rho,sigma}.

The garbled passage reads approximately: 'qui n'est qu'une explicitation de ce fait surprenant(*) que les diagrammes analogues (95) ... sont obtenus par celui-ci', with a marginal insertion ('... mod pas entièrement'?) and a footnote mark (*).
(107) reads approximately: 'groupe T_{rho,sigma}, et les homs. T_{rho,sigma} --χ--> G_m, T_{rho,sigma} --(ε_3, ε_2)--> μ_2 x μ_2'.
The 'groupes' before (108) belongs to the phrase 'en termes des groupes T_rho, N'_sigma et des T_rho --δ_rho--> G_m, N'_sigma --δ_sigma--> G_m, N'_sigma --ε_sigma--> μ_2'.
